fields.summary: Show data quality results in Data Explorer
fields.description:
Show the current Synergy data-quality report in the analyst Data Explorer so the dataset checks are visible before using its rankings.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Show a result for each check, with the source, scope and checked time.

  • Provide loading, empty, error and retry states.

  • Keep failed, missing and unsupported checks distinct from passing checks.

  • Require authenticated analyst access to the report and panel.

Recommendation warning flags remain under SCRUM-479.

fields.summary: Data & Ingestion Foundation
Test next-season PPP forecasts using previous-season data
fields.description:
Test PPP forecasts using only information available before each prediction, then compare them with later results that were not used to build the model.

This follows [SCRUM-476](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-476). The current calibration report uses a fixed Ridge model, trains on earlier seasons, and evaluates a later season. However, it also uses statistics from the season being evaluated, so it does not prove pre-game forecasting accuracy. This task adds a separate forecasting evaluation.

To complete this task:

* Define when the prediction is made and how far ahead it predicts. Record when every input would have been available.
* Build the inputs from earlier information only. Do not use future games, future seasons, or the results being predicted.
* Reserve later data for the final test. Use only earlier data to choose features and model settings and to fit scaling or other data preparation steps.
* Compare the forecast model with a baseline that follows the same timing rules, using the same untouched test rows. Report prediction errors, calibration, sample counts, and limitations.
* Add tests showing that changing future data cannot change earlier prediction inputs or data preparation fitted on earlier training data.
* Document the test procedure and code and dataset versions so someone else can reproduce the results.

fields.summary: Evaluation & Verification (Uplift/MAE/Calibration)
Keep production links on the public app address
fields.description:
Opening the production deployment address nbaplayranker-bxg9zds45-pearson-manufacturing.vercel.app causes API fetches to fail. Its CORS preflight returns 400 Disallowed CORS; the public address nbaplayranker-seven.vercel.app returns 200 and the backend is healthy.

Acceptance criteria:

  • New production deployments redirect to https://nbaplayranker-seven.vercel.app with a temporary 307.

  • Preserve the requested path and query string without a redirect loop.

  • Keep the public address, preview deployments and local development unchanged.

  • Verify the deployed routing and the analyst data-quality request.

Older immutable deployments keep their previous code. Use the public app address when sharing or opening the app.

fields.summary: Apply Assignment 1 feedback: Test Plan
One-person ownership leaves critical work without backup
fields.description: Only one person knows pulls/model/UI; bus factor = 1.

Mitigation Strategy.value: List primary and backup owners for the data pipeline, API, interface and deployment. Have the backup follow the clean-checkout steps and record what still depends on the primary owner.

fields.summary: Extra features delay required release work
fields.description: Fancy visuals or features added without time budget.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Prioritize the failing core workflows and required submission corrections. Put optional features in the backlog and agree which existing task moves out when a new task moves in.

fields.summary: Late requirement changes force rework
fields.description: Supervisor requests live data or extra models close to deadline.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Record each new requirement against its affected story, model or test. Estimate its effect on the remaining schedule and confirm scope changes in the shared plan.

fields.summary: Coaches may not use or trust the recommendations
fields.description: Tool isn’t used due to complexity or lack of trust.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Observe scouting, matchup and late-game scenarios with a coach or identified proxy. Record confusing steps and whether the result supports a concrete decision.

fields.summary: Protected APIs may allow unauthorized access
fields.description:
Risk: Application or API operations intended for authenticated or authorized users may remain accessible without the required session or role.  
Trigger: An unauthenticated, expired-session, or wrong-role request succeeds where the approved access policy requires rejection.  
Assessment: Low probability is retained provisionally; propose Serious impact because the current model includes authenticated coach/analyst access. Endpoint reduction alone does not establish authorization.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Maintain a route and role matrix. Repeat missing-session, invalid-token and wrong-role checks after access changes, and restrict any route that accepts an unauthorized request.

fields.summary: Private tokens may be exposed in source or logs
fields.description: Auth token or keys committed to Git or exposed in logs.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Scan tracked changes and client output before sharing a release. Store server keys only in private configuration and rotate any key whose exposure is confirmed.

fields.summary: Exported values may differ from API results
fields.description: JSON responses differ from CSV/Parquet due to version drift or rounding.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use the same calculation and filters for each output format. Compare JSON, CSV and PDF values on a fixed dataset and record the dataset version with the export test.

fields.summary: Missing models may break the baseline fallback
fields.description: If ML fails, baseline isn’t used automatically, causing outages.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Test a controlled missing-model case outside production. Confirm the supported baseline fallback and show a clear error for workflows that cannot safely fall back.

fields.summary: Core pages may fail on supported browsers or screen sizes
fields.description:
Risk: New interface changes may cause clipping, inaccessible controls, or broken workflows on supported browsers and screen sizes.  
Trigger: A supported browser or viewport cannot complete a core task or displays unreadable/overlapping content.  
Assessment: historical UI testing does not cover later changes.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Choose supported browser and viewport combinations, then repeat login, explorer, ranking and export flows. Fix clipped controls and unreadable results before expanding the supported set.

fields.summary: Gameplan inputs may be ignored or incorrectly validated
fields.description:
Risk: Unsupported seasons, team selections, context values, or limits may pass validation and cause errors or misleading rankings.  
Trigger: An invalid or unsupported input is accepted silently, causes an unhandled exception, or returns misleading output.  
Assessment: one invalid request should not produce unsupported analytics.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use one validated parsed context for every downstream request. Add first-click, boundary, overtime and unsupported-input cases and keep the failing case linked to its repair.

fields.summary: Recommendation explanations may be unclear
fields.description: Rationale text is too technical or long; causes confusion.

Mitigation Strategy.value: State when a recommendation uses baseline data without game context. Keep each explanation tied to displayed values, repeat BST-97–99 after the change and ask a reviewer to explain the recommendation and its limits.

fields.summary: Deployed analysis requests exceed usable response times
fields.description: Baseline >2s or ML >5s harms usability during short breaks.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Serve saved evaluation results for ordinary page visits. Profile slow requests, set bounded loading and error states, and rerun the recorded timeout case after the fix.

fields.summary: Metric labels may imply unsupported accuracy
fields.description:
Risk: PPP, MAE, RMSE, uplift, accuracy, or probability may be conflated, causing incorrect interpretation of results.  
Trigger: The report, API, or UI gives different meanings or units for the same metric, or labels a regression metric as classification accuracy.  
Assessment: definitions must match the actual prediction target and evaluation task.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use consistent units and definitions in the API, page and report. Show the prediction target, baseline and evaluation period alongside each result.

fields.summary: Parsed context may not reach the ranking model
fields.description:
Risk: Situational variables may be incomplete, noisy, or inappropriate for the target, weakening contextual recommendations.  
Trigger: Features have poor coverage, unstable definitions, or no defensible contribution on held-out evaluation.  
Assessment: the historical comment explicitly retained this concern.

Mitigation Strategy.value: List each context field and its availability, validation and use in ranking. Pass supported fields consistently and label unsupported conditions rather than implying they affect the result.

fields.summary: Poor calibration of predicted PPP
fields.description: Predicted PPP is systematically higher/lower than realized PPP.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Track PPP bias and error by season and play type. Evaluate lagged predictors on untouched chronological holdouts before making forecasting claims; report small groups and unsupported results.

fields.summary: Models may overfit the available data
fields.description: Model learns noise due to many features vs samples, hurting generalization.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Compare training and untouched time-holdout error with strictly available predictors. Record model settings, sample size and baseline performance before changing model complexity.

fields.summary: Data leakage inflates results
fields.description: Not using strict time splits leaks future info into training, inflating metrics.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Define the prediction moment and whether each feature is observed, lagged or supplied as a planned action. Fit preprocessing on training data only and use an untouched time holdout. Do not present conditional or retrospective estimates as prospective accuracy.

fields.summary: ML model underperforms the baseline
fields.description: XGBoost shows no uplift over the transparent scoring rule.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Evaluate baseline and model on identical untouched examples. Report error and uncertainty, and retain the better-supported method when model gains are absent.

fields.summary: Shot events may be assigned to the wrong team
fields.description: Timestamps/events don’t align cleanly with team/play-type rows; context features become noisy.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Recover authoritative raw events, map game participants explicitly and check team/opponent consistency. Rebuild derived shot data and verify samples against their raw events before trusting shot rankings.

fields.summary: Small-sample play types distort rankings
fields.description: Rare play types have few possessions and appear misleadingly strong/weak.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Define a minimum possession threshold and test low-count groups. Show sample size or suppress unsupported rankings; do not treat extreme small-sample PPP as a strong recommendation.

fields.summary: Player-to-team aggregation may calculate incorrect totals
fields.description: Possession-weighted aggregation implemented incorrectly, skewing team stats.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use known player rows to verify team possession totals and weighted PPP. Check duplicate player/team keys and compare the computed aggregate with the expected team result.

fields.summary: Invalid source data may produce misleading results
fields.description: Non-numeric fields, NAs, or duplicates lead to wrong PPP or frequency values.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Validate game participants, team/opponent differences and expected shooting-team coverage as well as types and missing values. Block or visibly flag reports using failed data.

fields.summary: Source changes may prevent dataset recovery
fields.description: hoopR/NBA tables or columns change (schema/rate limits), causing pulls or processing to fail.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Keep raw extracts with source and schema versions. Validate required fields before replacing a working dataset, and retain the previous release for rollback.

fields.summary: Limited expert feedback leaves coaching assumptions untested
fields.description: The project may miss practical coaching requirements when domain feedback is unavailable or not recorded.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Prepare three realistic coaching scenarios and specific questions. Record the reviewer, feedback and resulting changes, or clearly record that feedback is still pending.

fields.summary: UI and API contracts may disagree
fields.description: A page may send parameters, expect fields or allow roles that disagree with the backend contract.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Keep the failed browser cases linked to their bugs. Verify parameters, access roles and response fields from the real page through the deployed API after each repair.

fields.summary: Preprocessing may assign incorrect shot participants
fields.description: Incorrect data mappings or cleaning rules may produce misleading features and recommendations.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Replace ambiguous column matching with explicit documented mappings. Preserve raw events, validate participants and row counts after each transform, and rebuild dependent artifacts only from verified input.

fields.summary: Unplanned features compete with the agreed scope
fields.description: New features may consume the time reserved for agreed release requirements and defect fixes.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Track required work in the release plan and keep enhancements separate. Review additions against capacity and the remaining defects before promising a release date.

fields.summary: The model may not improve on the baseline
fields.description:
The ML model may not improve on the baseline for the intended prediction task.  
Trigger: held-out results show no useful improvement or unacceptable errors.  
Assessment: High probability and Serious impact are retained pending the current evaluation.  
Inception lesson: the existing review compares PPP predictions with the baseline using RMSE.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Compare model and baseline on the same prediction task and held-out period. Diagnose feature and data problems before tuning, and report a lack of improvement when that is the result.

fields.summary: Upstream schema changes may break dataset reloads
fields.description: This would trigger: columns missing, API failures

Mitigation Strategy.value: Pin the source tooling and validate columns, types and participant keys on a staged pull. Publish only a passing dataset version and retain the previous version for rollback.

fields.summary: Seasonal data changes may distort comparisons
fields.description: This would trigger: PPP ranges shift, sudden distribution changes

Mitigation Strategy.value: Record row counts, coverage and metric ranges by season. Investigate changes before training or comparing seasons, and include the dataset version and exclusions in the report.

fields.summary: Rare play types may produce unstable rankings
fields.description: This will trigger: very low possessions for a play type

Mitigation Strategy.value: Test rare play types with low possession counts and ties. Apply the agreed threshold or weighting consistently and show the sample limitation with the result.

fields.summary: An absence may leave critical tasks without coverage
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Team member reports illness, reduced availability, or misses a planned work session
* Tasks start slipping or are left unassigned for 24–48 hours
* No progress updates on assigned stories/subtasks

Impact on project:

* Reduced sprint capacity and missed sprint goals
* Rework or rushed work leading to defects
* Delays to dependent tasks and integration

Mitigation Strategy.value: Record weekly availability and the critical dependencies affected by an absence. Agree any reassignment and reduce optional work when capacity drops.

fields.summary: Exam weeks may reduce planned capacity
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Exam schedule overlaps sprint timeline
* Reduced commits/updates or delayed responses
* Teammate flags limited hours for the week

Impact on project:

* Lower throughput and incomplete sprint scope
* Increased load on other members and burnout risk
* Delays to deliverables tied to iteration deadlines

Mitigation Strategy.value: Record known exam and workload constraints before assigning the week. Split large tasks and defer lower-priority work when confirmed capacity is insufficient.

fields.summary: Cancelled meetings may leave decisions unresolved
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* A scheduled meeting is cancelled or multiple members cannot attend
* Decisions are blocked (scope, priorities, technical approach)
* No shared sprint check-in occurs

Impact on project:

* Misalignment on priorities and duplicated work
* Blocked tasks and delayed decisions
* Higher risk of sprint failure due to lack of coordination

Mitigation Strategy.value: Record the agenda and unanswered decisions in the shared plan. Agree a response time and alternative meeting or written decision process, then update the dependent tasks.

fields.summary: Missing stakeholder feedback may delay validation
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Stakeholder does not respond to messages or can’t attend planned feedback session
* Feedback is delayed beyond the sprint timeline
* Uncertainty remains about expected UX/output

Impact on project:

* Risk of building the wrong thing or missing expectations
* Slower iteration cycles and delayed validation
* Increased rework close to demo/defense time

Mitigation Strategy.value: Prepare a short scenario review with clear questions and an agreed response date. If a proxy reviews it, identify that limitation and keep unanswered stakeholder questions open.

fields.summary: New features may exceed the release scope
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* New features keep being added without removing/deferring others
* Sprint backlog expands after sprint start
* “Nice-to-have” items replace core deliverables

Impact on project:

* Missed sprint goals and late releases
* Reduced quality due to rushing
* Harder to deliver a stable demo and complete documentation

Mitigation Strategy.value: Require a clear outcome and acceptance criteria before adding work to the current iteration. Agree a displaced item whenever an urgent addition exceeds available capacity.

fields.summary: Sprint commitments may exceed available capacity
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Sprint has too many high-point stories or large unknowns
* Multiple stories remain “In Progress” late in the sprint
* Work spills over sprint-to-sprint regularly

Impact on project:

* Lower completion rate and morale
* Increased unfinished work and messy backlog
* Rushed implementation and more defects

Mitigation Strategy.value: Review unfinished tasks, dependencies and capacity at the start of each week. Split large items and leave room for integration failures instead of assuming every planned item will finish.

fields.summary: Uncertain tasks may take longer than estimated
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Tasks take significantly longer than estimated
* Frequent “unknown unknowns” during implementation
* Many subtasks added mid-work to finish a story

Impact on project:

* Sprint goals missed due to inaccurate planning
* Increased overtime/rushing and quality issues
* Unreliable release forecasting

Mitigation Strategy.value: Break uncertain work into a bounded investigation and a repair task. Re-estimate after the investigation, and record actual effort without adding guessed hours.

fields.summary: Project work may be unevenly distributed
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* One member consistently has more assigned/closed issues than others
* PR history shows one person doing most key work
* Some members are repeatedly unassigned or doing only minor tasks

Impact on project:

* Academic evaluation risk (team contribution concerns)
* Knowledge siloing and bus-factor risk increases
* Burnout for one member and lower team morale

Mitigation Strategy.value: Review task ownership, completed changes and actual worklogs with both members. Arrange backup coverage without claiming or reassigning another member's work.

fields.summary: Shared-main integration may break working features
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Frequent merge conflicts or failed merges
* Main branch build/tests fail after merges
* Features break after integration (regressions)

Impact on project:

* Development slows due to rework and debugging
* Risk of unstable demo build
* Lost time during sprint end when integration matters most

Mitigation Strategy.value: Fetch and inspect shared changes before integrating. Run relevant tests and a build for substantive changes, push to the shared repository and keep a known deployment rollback point.

fields.summary: GitHub or Jira outages may interrupt project work
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* GitHub or Jira is temporarily unavailable
* PR merges blocked or Jira updates cannot be logged
* Team cannot access boards or repositories

Impact on project:

* Short-term productivity loss and delayed merges
* Missing tracking information for the day
* Risk of losing sprint visibility temporarily

Mitigation Strategy.value: Keep a usable shared-repository clone and dated Jira exports. During an outage, record actual work locally and reconcile it once access returns without inventing historical timestamps.

fields.summary: Low disk space may block builds and recovery
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Device errors, low storage warnings, or frequent crashes
* Build tools fail due to insufficient disk space
* Slow performance prevents testing or running workloads

Impact on project:

* Development delays and inability to contribute
* Risk of losing local work if not committed
* Missed deadlines due to blocked environment

Mitigation Strategy.value: Check free disk space before builds and preserve uncommitted work. Remove only confirmed disposable files, then verify a clean build and keep setup instructions usable on another machine.

fields.summary: Missing credentials may block service recovery
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Environment variables missing/incorrect
* Locked out of cloud services or hosting accounts
* API calls fail due to expired/revoked keys

Impact on project:

* Deployment blocked or system non-functional
* Risk of downtime during demo period
* Potential security incident if keys are mishandled

Mitigation Strategy.value: List service owners and recovery contacts without recording secrets. Verify required access and document key rotation or environment-update steps for an expired credential.

fields.summary: Unclear acceptance criteria may cause rework
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Conflicting instructions or changing expectations
* Stories lack acceptance criteria or success definition
* Team debates what “done” means late in sprint

Impact on project:

* Rework and wasted development time
* Misaligned deliverables relative to rubric/expectations
* Lower quality due to frequent changes

Mitigation Strategy.value: Add clear inputs, expected outcomes and failure behavior to each story. Link the implementation and tests, and record scope changes when requirements differ from the existing work.

fields.summary: Unrecorded team decisions may block integration
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Teammates unsure what others are working on
* Duplicate work or conflicting implementations
* Delays in responding to blockers or questions

Impact on project:

* Reduced velocity and wasted effort
* Integration conflicts and inconsistent design decisions
* Higher stress and risk of missed deadlines

Mitigation Strategy.value: Agree a response window and record blockers on the affected task. Confirm decisions and ownership changes explicitly, then update the shared plan.

fields.summary: Critical areas may depend on one team member
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* One person owns most complex modules (ML/FE/frontend/deploy)
* Documentation is missing for critical setup or pipelines
* Others cannot run or modify key parts confidently

Impact on project:

* High risk if that member becomes unavailable
* Slower progress due to dependency on one person
* Harder to debug issues under time pressure

Mitigation Strategy.value: Document the pipeline and deployment steps and have the backup owner run them. Record unanswered questions and the next handoff needed for each critical area.

fields.summary: Setup and tooling failures may delay development
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Frequent build/install failures or dependency issues
* Environment differences cause “works on my machine” problems
* Significant time spent on setup rather than feature work

Impact on project:

* Lower output and delayed milestones
* Increased frustration and rushed implementation
* Demo instability if environments are inconsistent

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use the active shared checkout and pinned dependency instructions. Record reproducible setup failures, address disk constraints and verify the environment before planning a release build.

fields.summary: Missing submission artifacts may put the deadline at risk
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Deadlines not tracked or unclear ownership for admin work
* Deliverables (reports, boards, links) not updated weekly
* Sprint completion tasks get skipped

Impact on project:

* Grade penalties and missed evaluation requirements
* Incomplete documentation for defense
* Last-minute scramble increases error risk

Mitigation Strategy.value: Maintain a checklist of required artifacts, owners and due dates. Verify live links, native model files and individual evidence before the team submits the package.

fields.summary: Shot-data mapping may produce invalid game participants
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Dataset2 columns do not match expected names/types
* Ingestion/ETL script fails or produces many nulls after mapping
* Joins/keys don’t align with dataset1 or unified schema

Impact on project:

* Dataset2 cannot be used for training/analysis
* Delays ML pipeline updates and dashboard integration
* Increased rework to redesign the schema mapping layer

Mitigation Strategy.value: Document the raw-to-processed field mapping and validate participant IDs, opponent IDs and row counts. Reject a staged dataset that fails these checks and retain the unaffected play-type workflow.

fields.summary: Missing raw fields may prevent reliable shot features
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Required fields for your features are absent (e.g., context variables, matchup identifiers)
* You cannot compute existing feature set consistently for dataset2
* Dashboard views or model inputs become incomplete

Impact on project:

* Reduced feature set and weaker model/explanations
* Inconsistent outputs between dataset1 and dataset2
* Extra work required to redesign features or UI expectations

Mitigation Strategy.value: Recover authoritative raw events and verify required game, participant, clock and margin fields. Report missing or unmapped columns, preserve missingness instead of presenting fabricated ties and disable any feature that cannot be calculated reliably.

fields.summary: Shot-data quality failures may reach users
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* High missingness in critical columns
* Duplicate records or non-unique keys
* IDs/labels inconsistent across tables (team IDs, player IDs, game IDs)

Impact on project:

* Incorrect aggregations and misleading analytics
* Model performance drops due to noisy inputs
* Time loss debugging issues that look like “model bugs” but are data issues

Mitigation Strategy.value: Add semantic participant checks to the quality report and show failed status in the explorer. Keep raw and processed data separate and record all exclusions or replacements.

fields.summary: Model results may drift between seasons
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Metric distributions shift across seasons (pace, efficiency, play-type frequency)
* Model accuracy changes significantly when evaluating different seasons
* Dashboards show inconsistent baselines between time ranges

Impact on project:

* Less stable performance and harder-to-compare results
* Explanations may change meaning across seasons
* Confusing results for users when switching time windows

Mitigation Strategy.value: Track feature distributions and error by season using fixed definitions. Investigate meaningful shifts before retraining and state which periods support each result.

fields.summary: Missing source provenance may prevent reproducible features
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Re-running pipeline produces different features/results unexpectedly
* Feature code depends on manual steps or local-only conditions
* Feature generation lacks versioning or saved artifacts

Impact on project:

* Hard to justify results and model choice
* Debugging becomes very time-consuming
* Risk of demo/report mismatch (“numbers changed”)

Mitigation Strategy.value: Keep raw input, transformation code and configuration together under a dataset version. Record hashes and expected counts, then rebuild and compare derived features from that version.

fields.summary: The second dataset may reduce model performance
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Evaluation metrics worsen compared to dataset1 baseline
* Model becomes unstable across folds/splits
* Feature importance shifts dramatically with dataset2

Impact on project:

* Harder to justify adding dataset2
* Reduced recommendation quality and weaker demo credibility
* Extra time needed for tuning and feature adjustments

Mitigation Strategy.value: Evaluate the original, second-dataset and combined methods on matched held-out cases after data repair. Report where added data helps or harms the result and retain the supported baseline.

fields.summary: Models may fail on new games or seasons
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Training performance is high but validation/test performance is poor
* Large gap between train and test metrics
* Model predictions unstable across different splits

Impact on project:

* Recommendations not reliable in new scenarios
* Explanations may be misleading if model is not generalizing
* Risk of poor demo outcomes depending on sample

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use untouched chronological holdouts and fit preprocessing on training rows only. Compare train and test error, sample counts and variation across periods before choosing model complexity.

fields.summary: Model explanations may be difficult to justify
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Model metrics are acceptable but explanations are unclear or inconsistent
* Stakeholders ask “why?” and response relies on vague reasoning
* Feature importance results are unstable or hard to translate to coaching language

Impact on project:

* Low trust and adoption of recommendations
* Defence risk: weak justification of model choice
* Harder to connect outputs to decision-making

Mitigation Strategy.value: Show the selected play, supporting metric and relevant limitation. Compare alternative recommendations and collect feedback on whether the explanation matches the displayed evidence.

fields.summary: Training during page loads may cause timeouts
fields.description:
Slow processing, training, or recommendation requests may delay work or cause timeouts.  
Trigger: the workflow exceeds its agreed timing target or times out.  
Assessment: Moderate probability; Serious impact because delays can make the application unusable.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Precompute and store evaluation artifacts instead of training on an ordinary page visit. Bound expensive work and verify the page can display saved results or a clear unavailable state.

fields.summary: Dashboard requests may stall or repeat expensive work
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Charts take several seconds to load or time out
* Queries run repeatedly on the same data
* Frontend shows loading spinners frequently

Impact on project:

* Poor user experience and demo risk
* Stakeholders perceive the system as incomplete
* Harder to explore insights interactively

Mitigation Strategy.value: Separate request state by resource, remove duplicate initial evaluation and serve cached metrics. Test loading, success and error states with the actual page requests.

fields.summary: Charts may fail to render or misrepresent their context
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Users misinterpret results or draw wrong conclusions
* Charts hide important context (sample size, variance)
* Too many metrics shown without explanation

Impact on project:

* Incorrect decision-making support
* Lower trust in the system
* Defence risk if visuals are not defensible

Mitigation Strategy.value: Render the actual response through the page before reviewing the chart. Show metric units, filters, period and sample size, then record what decision the chart helps the user make.

fields.summary: Displayed results may disagree with API data
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* UI values don’t match backend logs or expected calculations
* Different filters produce inconsistent totals
* “Same query” returns different numbers across endpoints

Impact on project:

* Loss of credibility and debugging time
* Incorrect explanations and rankings
* Demo risk due to inconsistent outputs

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use a shared typed request and response contract. Test displayed values and context against the exact successful API response, including missing sections and error cases.

fields.summary: Dataset mapping errors may corrupt team statistics
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Join keys mismatch (game/team/player IDs not aligned)
* Row counts explode or collapse unexpectedly after joining
* Derived outputs look unrealistic (extreme metrics, missing teams)

Impact on project:

* Incorrect dashboards and model training data
* High debugging time and reduced trust
* Potentially invalid conclusions in the report

Mitigation Strategy.value: Validate joins using explicit game and participant keys. Check row-count changes, both participants and team/opponent consistency against raw events before publishing derived data.

fields.summary: Missing runtime features may break inference
fields.description:
Missing or incompatible runtime inputs may cause recommendation requests to fail.  
Trigger: required fields are missing, inputs have the wrong format, or model/prediction data is unavailable.  
Assessment: Moderate probability; Serious impact because core requests can fail.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Validate required feature fields at the API boundary and check artifact compatibility at startup. Test missing inputs and artifacts with a clear rejection or documented fallback.

fields.summary: Future generated explanations may invent unsupported facts
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Explanations mention stats not present in the computed payload
* Explanation contradicts displayed values
* Different runs produce inconsistent “reasons” for same input

Impact on project:

* Trust damage and adoption risk
* Incorrect coaching guidance
* Defence risk: explanation system appears unreliable

Mitigation Strategy.value: Supply only validated ranked plays and evidence. Reject invented references or contradictory claims and retain the template response whenever the generated output cannot be validated.

fields.summary: Future explanation API costs may exceed an agreed budget
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Requests fail due to rate limits
* LLM responses are slow or time out
* Costs exceed budget or usage limits

Impact on project:

* Explanation feature unavailable during demo
* UI appears incomplete or broken
* Increased stress close to deadlines

Mitigation Strategy.value: Obtain a separate provider budget before activation. Limit requests and output size, cache repeated scenarios, set an application cutoff and keep templates available when the provider fails.

fields.summary: Future generated explanations may be vague or inconsistent
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Explanations repeat generic phrases without referencing specifics
* Two similar inputs get very different explanations
* Stakeholders say explanations are not helpful

Impact on project:

* Reduced perceived value of explanation feature
* Lower trust and adoption
* Harder to justify “advanced CS” value in defence

Mitigation Strategy.value: Evaluate repeated and contrasting scenarios against reference facts. Require a concrete reason and limitation, reject unsupported detail and keep the wording aligned with the glossary.

fields.summary: Server credentials may leak into client output
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Keys appear in frontend code, console logs, or client network responses
* Secrets are committed to repo or included in build artifacts
* Unauthorized access attempts or suspicious usage appears

Impact on project:

* Credential compromise and potential service misuse
* Forced rotation of keys and possible downtime
* Serious compliance/security concern in demo/report

Mitigation Strategy.value: Inspect tracked changes and generated client output for private credentials. Keep server secrets server-side, restrict their permissions and rotate any confirmed exposure.

fields.summary: Deployment settings may not match the tested release
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* App works locally but fails after deployment
* Missing environment variables or wrong URLs
* CORS/auth settings differ between local and deployed env

Impact on project:

* Deployment downtime and demo risk
* Debugging time lost late in sprint
* Inconsistent behavior across environments

Mitigation Strategy.value: Keep a variable-name checklist and deployment manifest. Verify endpoint URLs, auth settings and startup data on the selected release, then run smoke checks before changing traffic.

fields.summary: Changed API contracts may break existing pages
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Frontend expects fields that backend no longer returns
* Endpoint parameters change without coordinated update
* Frequent 4xx/5xx responses after merges

Impact on project:

* Features break unexpectedly
* Increased debugging and rework
* Demo reliability decreases

Mitigation Strategy.value: Link each failing page/API contract to a bug and test. Verify parameter names, response fields and roles together before closing the failure.

fields.summary: Insufficient workflow tests may miss regressions
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Bugs reappear after changes
* No consistent regression checklist at sprint end
* New features break old ones without detection

Impact on project:

* Unstable demo and user experience
* Increased time spent firefighting instead of building
* Lower confidence in final release quality

Mitigation Strategy.value: Add feature-linked Fall 2026 cases, put them on the board and execute them against a named release. Preserve failures, create specific bugs and rerun the failing case after a fix.

fields.summary: The deployed demo may fail despite local tests
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Differences between local and demo environment (data paths, env vars, ports)
* Demo machine lacks dependencies or uses different versions
* Performance issues only appear in deployed environment

Impact on project:

* High demo/defense risk
* Last-minute debugging and reduced confidence
* Stakeholders perceive project as incomplete

Mitigation Strategy.value: Run the intended demo path against the deployed release, including sign-in, actual downloads and analysis pages. Keep a fallback path and record any feature that is unavailable.

fields.summary: Recommendations may lack convincing evidence
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Stakeholders ask “Why is this recommended?” and the system cannot answer clearly
* Feedback indicates explanations are unclear, generic, or inconsistent
* Users ignore or distrust ranked outputs even if they look correct

Impact on project:

* Low adoption and reduced perceived value of the solution
* Defence risk: unclear justification of decision-support capability
* Higher rework to retrofit explanations late in the project

Mitigation Strategy.value: Show the evidence behind the selected play and the limits of the comparison. Ask a reviewer to explain why it ranks highly and record any unsupported or unclear claim.

fields.summary: The workflow may not support practical coaching tasks
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Stakeholders say outputs are interesting but not actionable for game prep
* The system requires too many steps to get to a useful conclusion
* Filters/labels don’t match how coaches think (time, lineup, opponent, situation)

Impact on project:

* Lower adoption and weaker stakeholder satisfaction
* Extra time needed to redesign UI and outputs
* Defence risk if the solution appears “academic” rather than practical

Mitigation Strategy.value: Walk through scouting, matchup preparation and a late-game choice. Record extra steps, missing context and whether the user can turn the result into a useful plan.

fields.summary: Charts may not support a clear coaching decision
fields.description:
Charts may show statistics without helping users decide what to run or defend.  
Trigger: users cannot explain the decision supported by a chart.  
Assessment: Moderate probability; Serious impact because unclear charts reduce the system's usefulness.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Give each chart one clear comparison and show its period, filters and sample size. Record reviewer feedback and link any resulting visualization changes.

fields.summary: The defence may overstate unmeasured project impact
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Difficulty explaining “why this matters” beyond technical implementation
* Demo shows features but not outcomes or measurable benefits
* Report lacks clear success metrics, scenarios, or evaluation evidence

Impact on project:

* Lower evaluation scores due to unclear impact
* Weak narrative in defence/presentation
* Stakeholders do not understand the value proposition

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use concrete scenarios and measured outcomes where available. Explain the baseline, evaluation limits and user task without inventing time saved or performance gains.

fields.summary: The project may lack a supported comparison with existing tools
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Review of existing tools shows similar dashboards/reports
* Stakeholders ask “How is this different from X?”
* Project description sounds generic (stats dashboard only)

Impact on project:

* Reduced perceived novelty and lower stakeholder interest
* Defence risk if differentiation is not articulated
* Harder to justify “advanced CS” component

Mitigation Strategy.value: Compare the current supported features and evaluation approach with relevant tools. Cite the comparison and describe specific differences without claiming novelty that has not been established.

fields.summary: Technical language may confuse coaches
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* UI includes ML/stat terms without translation
* Stakeholders struggle to understand metric meaning or navigation
* Feedback indicates the tool feels complex or “engineering-focused”

Impact on project:

* Lower adoption and less trust in outputs
* Increased training/support required to use the tool
* Defence risk if the solution isn’t accessible to the target user

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use short labels and definitions, keep the main task simple and place detail behind optional views. Ask the reviewer to interpret the result and record terms that need rewriting.

fields.summary: Statistics may be interpreted as unsupported personal judgments
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Stakeholders worry about fairness/bias in interpreting player/team performance
* Explanations sound too definitive (“this player is bad”) without uncertainty
* Outputs may be misused as “truth” rather than decision support

Impact on project:

* Reduced trust and stakeholder concerns in defence
* Risk of misinterpretation causing reputational harm (even in academic context)
* Requirement to add disclaimers/limitations late in project

Mitigation Strategy.value: Use evidence-based wording, sample sizes and evaluation limits. Remove unsupported personal judgments and make clear where an output is only decision support.

fields.summary: Incomplete model and test evidence may weaken the defence
fields.description:
Trigger / Early Warning Signs:

* Documentation lags behind implementation
* Demo steps are unclear or not rehearsed
* Report misses required sections or lacks evidence/screenshots

Impact on project:

* Lower defence score even if the product works
* Increased last-minute work and errors
* Harder for evaluators to understand and verify the solution

Mitigation Strategy.value: Keep the report, native model and Jira links aligned with actual changes. Demonstrate the tested release, preserve failed results and include each member's real contribution evidence.

fields.summary: Delayed responses may leave task dependencies unresolved
fields.description:
Risk: An extended lack of response may leave task ownership, dependencies, or project decisions unresolved.  
Trigger: A teammate does not respond within the agreed response window and a recorded project decision or dependency is blocked.  
Assessment: response expectations and escalation should be agreed rather than treating silence as consent.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Agree a response window and backup contact. Record the affected task when a response is overdue and seek explicit agreement before changing ownership.

fields.summary: Missing runtime artifacts may break a new deployment
fields.description: After a restart or deployment, the app may be unable to find the data, model predictions or saved state it needs. This could stop recommendations from loading. The proposed rating is Moderate probability and Serious impact. This describes a possible failure; the original review did not find that an outage had occurred.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Version runtime data, model files and configuration together. Validate production prerequisites with clear diagnostics, distinguish liveness from readiness and verify recovery from a clean checkout before replacing the release.

fields.summary: Dataset reuse terms may restrict sharing
fields.description:
Dataset reuse or sharing conditions may not permit the project's intended use.  
Trigger: permission for acquisition, hosting, outputs, or redistribution is unclear or unsuitable.  
Proposed assessment: Low probability; Serious impact because the affected data or output may need to be replaced. No violation is established by this review.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Record each source and its applicable terms. Resolve unclear reuse or sharing permissions and use a permitted replacement or narrower distribution when necessary.

fields.summary: Hosting costs or billing interruptions may stop the backend
fields.description:
Billing was reactivated and the backend passed its live checks. The project has a CAD$10 monthly budget and a CAD$7 Cloud Run spending control, but delayed billing data and other service costs mean these are not a guarantee of the total bill.

Originally, the free trial had expired and a hosting plan still needed to be agreed. The risk was rated Very High probability and Serious impact because hosting costs or a billing interruption could delay development, testing and demos. Actual charges and backend availability had not yet been checked at that point.

Continue monitoring for rising costs, expired credits or billing problems that could interrupt the backend.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Review project charges by service against the CAD10 budget. Keep scale-to-zero and the existing controls, and plan a backed-up migration or reduced-cost fallback if the forecast exceeds the agreed budget.

fields.summary: Visual Paradigm compatibility may block shared model updates
fields.description:
The corrected deployment diagram is published in VP revision 55. The shared copy contains the new layout and protocol-port labels.

A version mismatch previously blocked an import, and the command-line commit tool later failed. Desktop Team Commit worked. Future version mismatches could still interrupt imports or sharing, so this risk stays under monitoring.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Back up the native project before updating Visual Paradigm. Check that team members use compatible versions. Use Desktop Team Commit and check the shared revision after publishing.

fields.summary: Free-plan limits or inactivity may pause Supabase
fields.description:
After Basketball Playtype Ranker resumed on the Free plan, the sign-in, profile-permission and Gameplan database checks passed.

Originally, the project was paused and could not resume because an owner or administrator had reached the limit of two active free projects. The reason for the original pause was not confirmed. The risk was rated Very High probability and Serious impact because unavailable database and sign-in services could delay testing and demos, and restoring access might require an agreed paid plan.

The dashboard reported that data and backups were safe, with June 1, 2027 shown as the deadline to resume that paused project. It said the project could not resume after that date, but the data would still be available to download. No data loss was reported.

Continue checking project availability and free-project capacity before demonstrations and after inactivity.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Check project status and sign-in before the demo, preserve backups and identify the service owner. Do not upgrade a plan or pause another owner's project without the required agreement.

fields.summary: Fix shot-team attribution and rebuild the shot dataset
fields.description:
The shot data has incorrect team labels: 18,746 rows list the same team and opponent, and all 7,520 games with at least 100 shots show only one shooting team. A TOR 2025-26 export also had 51 invalid rows out of 5,000.

To reproduce, run backend/tests/test_shot_attribution_regression.py with --runxfail and compare the TOR/BOS input events with the output team, opponent and home flag.

Acceptance criteria:

* Use explicit participant IDs to identify the shooting team. Changing a score must not change the team.
* Recover the original event data and rebuild the cleaned dataset and derived files.
* Pass the row and game checks and compare samples with the original events before relying on shot results.

fields.summary: Data & Ingestion Foundation
Use the new Gameplan situation on the first Build
fields.description:
The first Gameplan Build uses the previous game situation. Clicking Build again uses the new values and changes the rankings.

To reproduce, start with TOR/BOS 2024-25, Q4, 180 seconds and margin -2. Enter "Q4 down 5 with 0:28 left", then click Build twice without changing anything.

Acceptance criteria:

* The first request and the page both use period 4, 28 seconds and margin -5.
* Pass the parsed situation directly into the ranking request.
* Add a test showing that unchanged inputs give the first and second builds the same context.

fields.summary: Coach UI & Tactics Board
Pass supported coaching conditions into Gameplan ranking
fields.description:
Gameplan recognizes phrases such as "Need a three" and "They are switching", but only sends numeric context to the ranking API.

To reproduce, enter those conditions and compare the parsed values with the request built by GameplanClient.

Acceptance criteria:

* Define which coaching conditions the ranker supports.
* Send supported conditions to the API and test their effect.
* Clearly show when a condition is unsupported and does not affect the ranking.

fields.summary: Context-Aware Re-Ranking (Score/Time/Recent Events)
Preserve overtime in the Gameplan context
fields.description:
Gameplan changes overtime to quarter 4 before ranking.

To reproduce, enter an overtime situation, build the plan and compare the parser result with the displayed period and ranking request.

Acceptance criteria:

* Keep the overtime period through parsing, display and ranking.
* Validate the overtime clock without changing the period.
* Add a test covering the complete parser-to-ranker path.

fields.summary: Context-Aware Re-Ranking (Score/Time/Recent Events)
Clear Model Metrics loading state when requests finish
fields.description:
Model Metrics keeps showing "Loading pipeline summary" and disables Refresh even after the holdout results appear.

To reproduce, sign in as an analyst, open Model Metrics and wait for the results table. The recorded run displayed Ridge RMSE 0.011 while the loading message remained.

Acceptance criteria:

* Track the summary and evaluation requests separately.
* Clear loading on success or error and allow a retry.
* Avoid duplicate initial requests and test loading, success and failure states.

fields.summary: Evaluation & Verification (Uplift/MAE/Calibration)
Load saved shot metrics without training during page requests
fields.description:
The default Shot Model Metrics request timed out after 300 seconds with HTTP 504 in the October 6 run. It has not been repeated during this revision.

Use the saved request and runtime results to investigate. After the fix, open the page once and record its result and response time.

Acceptance criteria:

* Load saved or precomputed metrics during normal page visits.
* Run expensive evaluation in a separate bounded job or preparation step.
* Show useful loading and error messages, and complete supported requests before the platform timeout.

fields.summary: Evaluation & Verification (Uplift/MAE/Calibration)
Align analyst shot pages with their API permissions
fields.description:
Analysts can open Shot Plan and Shot Heatmap, but their requests use coach-only APIs and return HTTP 403.

To reproduce, sign in as an analyst and run either page with a supported season and matchup.

Acceptance criteria:

* Decide which roles should use each page.
* Make navigation, page access and API permissions agree.
* Test allowed, wrong-role and signed-out access without opening unrelated coach-only routes.

fields.summary: Coach UI & Tactics Board
Render Shot Statistical Analysis using the current API fields
fields.description:
Shot Statistical Analysis receives a successful API response, then crashes while reading dropped.length. The response uses removed, and other page sections also expect older fields.

To reproduce, run the analysis as an analyst and compare the response with the fields used by the page.

Acceptance criteria:

* Update the types, response adapter and page components to match the API.
* Handle missing optional sections with an accurate unavailable message.
* Add a render test using a current response. Do not show results the API did not calculate.

fields.summary: Evaluation & Verification (Uplift/MAE/Calibration)
State when baseline explanations do not use game context
fields.description:
Baseline explanations do not say that score, period and clock were left out. BST-99 found this in all five returned explanations.

To reproduce, request baseline Top-K for 2024-25, TOR against BOS, K=5 without game context.

Acceptance criteria:

* Say when game context was not used.
* Keep context-based explanations tied to the values actually used.
* Rerun BST-97, BST-98 and BST-99 against the corrected code and deployment.

fields.summary: Data & Ingestion Foundation
Define backend readiness and explain missing prerequisites
fields.description:
A missing Synergy file produces a traceback. Missing Supabase settings still allow startup and /health 200, although protected requests remain blocked. The tests and app need a clear agreement on what "ready" means.

Acceptance criteria:

* Define startup requirements and separate running from ready to serve requests.
* Report missing data or auth settings clearly without exposing secrets.
* Do not report production readiness when required settings or data are absent.
* Keep development and isolated tests supported, then update and rerun BST-107 and BST-113.

fields.summary: Project Management & Support
Report unmapped shot-data columns during schema validation
fields.description:
BST-116 reports the missing TEAM_ABBR column but says nothing about an unused UNMAPPED_FIXTURE column. Extra metadata is allowed and is already excluded from model features.

Acceptance criteria:

* Report mapped, optional, ignored or unmapped, and missing required columns.
* Identify unused metadata without treating every extra column as an error.
* Keep missing-column errors clear and rerun both BST-116 examples.

fields.summary: Evaluation & Verification (Uplift/MAE/Calibration)
Validate shot margins and define when prediction inputs are available
fields.description:
All 1,332,515 retained shot rows have no MARGIN value, but model loading replaces it with zero. The app also needs to explain whether it predicts before a possession or evaluates a proposed shot.

Acceptance criteria:

* Recover real margins or show them as unavailable instead of treating missing values as tied scores.
* State when each prediction input becomes available.
* Use only prior information for pre-possession predictions. Define a separate input contract for a proposed-shot evaluation.
* After SCRUM-538 repairs the source data, rerun BST-117, BST-118 and BST-119 with finite-feature checks and later-season, per-fold results.

Related work: SCRUM-526.

fields.summary: Evaluation & Verification (Uplift/MAE/Calibration)
Set and verify the deployed Top-K response-time target
fields.description:
BST-111 needs an agreed response-time target. All eight test requests succeeded, but two took about 33 seconds with four running at once.

Acceptance criteria:

* Agree on a Top-K timing target, including cold starts and concurrent requests.
* Investigate slow requests using a limited test run and service logs.
* Rerun BST-111 and record the environment, sample size, target and p95 response time.
* Stay within the approved hosting budget.

fields.summary: Project Management & Support

sprints.name: Sprint 1 — Inception
sprints.goal:
As a coach, I can get a baseline Top-K from sample data so I see the concept working end-to-end.

Ship PSPI: UI nav + Data Explorer + Baseline Top-K (mock) + Context UI mock; VP wireframes/wireflow linked to UC steps.

sprints.goal: Breaking Down Capstone Project and Doing research on the topic

sprints.name: Iteration-2
sprints.goal: Assigning Roles and Breaking down approach

sprints.name: Iteration-3
sprints.goal: As an API client, I can request a validated baseline ranking so I can integrate it safely.

sprints.name: Iteration-4
sprints.goal: As a coach, I can view Top-K cards and print a one-page plan so I can use it pre-game.

sprints.name: Iteration-5
sprints.goal: As a coach, rankings consider basic game context so suggestions fit the flow.

sprints.name: Iteration-6
sprints.goal: As a supervisor, I see uplift vs baseline with a versioned model artifact.

sprints.name: Iteration-7
sprints.goal: As a supervisor, I see tests, logging, and /health so the baseline is stable to demo.

sprints.name: Iteration-8
sprints.goal: As a coach, I see plain-English rationales (feature importance) with each suggestion.

sprints.name: Iteration-10
sprints.goal: As a maintainer, I can run the cloud demo with auth, logs, and safe-mode.

sprints.name: Iteration-11
sprints.goal: As stakeholders, we can use a polished demo with exports and the final report.

sprints.name: Iteration-12
sprints.goal: Address what we have compared to feedback received from committee

sprints.name: Iteration-21
sprints.goal: System Hardening and Validation + Documentation and Project Finalization
